# Mathlib typos

_Generated by `scripts/typo_audit/typos.py` on 2026-10-08. 7692 findings across 3544 files._

The canonical record of every typo and consistency problem known in this repository.
Each finding is one row. Rows are identified by their category, token and file — not by
line number — so re-running the generator keeps whatever you have written into the
`Status` and `Note` columns, adds new findings as `open`, and drops findings that no
longer apply. **Triage by editing this file.**

Statuses: `open` (not yet looked at, or waiting for a maintainer's decision, which the
note states), `confirmed` (checked by hand, should be fixed), `fp` (false positive or
accepted exception), `fixed` (corrected; the row disappears on the next run), `wontfix`
(real but deliberately left alone). Confidence (`conf`) is the scanner's own estimate, not
a triage verdict. [`typo_triage.md`](typo_triage.md) records the rules rows are triaged by.

Current triage: **13 open**, 2988 confirmed, 3867 false positives, 824 wontfix.

[`tickets.md`](tickets.md) turns the open rows here into tickets, one pull request per
category and tier. Re-generate it whenever this file changes.

## How a finding gets here

Every surface is judged against the same yardstick: the vocabulary of Mathlib's own
comments. A word is reported only when the corpus never uses it, a dictionary does not
know it, it is not an identifier, it is not a regular derivative of a common word, and
some frequent word is one edit away. The corpus is built from comments under `Mathlib/`,
`Archive/` and `Counterexamples/` only, never from the surface being audited, so a typo
cannot vote itself into the dictionary. Everything that could otherwise be a matter of
taste — which spelling, which heading, which capitalisation — is settled by counting how
the rest of the library writes it, and those counts are in the `Detail` column.

## Declaration names

Findings about the names of declarations themselves — casing, Lean 3 spellings, outdated components, names that disagree with their statements. Generated by `scripts/naming_audit/naming_audit.py`.
